title: What is the superclass of all Java classes?
shortTitle: What is the superclass of all Java classes?
keyPoints: java.lang.Object is the root of every class hierarchy – every class extends Object implicitly
Object provides 11 methods: toString(), equals(), hashCode(), getClass(), clone(), finalize(), wait(), notify(), notifyAll(), plus 2 overloaded wait()
If you write class Account {}, it implicitly extends Object
You can override toString(), equals(), and hashCode() for meaningful behavior
getClass() returns the runtime class, useful for reflection and logging

s1_definition.oneliner: java.lang.Object is the implicit superclass of every Java class. It provides toString(), equals(), hashCode(), getClass(), clone(), wait(), notify(), and finalize().
s1_definition.profdef:
Object class facts:

- **Root of all classes.** Every class extends Object, even if not declared explicitly.
- **11 methods inherited** by every object: toString, equals, hashCode, getClass, clone, finalize (deprecated), wait (3 overloads), notify, notifyAll.
- **Default implementations:** toString returns className@hexHashCode, equals uses ==, hashCode returns a memory-based value.
s1_definition.analogy: Object is the standard bank form template. Every specific form (Account, Transaction) is based on this template, even if nobody explicitly says so. The template provides generic features like a form number (hashCode), a description field (toString), and an identity check (equals).

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  java.lang.Object
    │
    ├── toString()    → "Account@1a2b3c4d" (override for readability)
    ├── equals()      → == by default (override for value comparison)
    ├── hashCode()    → memory-based (override with equals)
    ├── getClass()    → runtime Class object
    ├── clone()       → shallow copy (prefer copy constructor)
    ├── finalize()    → deprecated, never use
    ├── wait()        → thread synchronization
    ├── notify()      → thread synchronization
    └── notifyAll()   → thread synchronization

  Every class extends Object implicitly.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
java.lang.Object is the root of every Java class. It provides default implementations of toString (class@hash), equals (reference comparison), hashCode (memory-based), and other methods. Override toString for readable output, equals for value comparison, and hashCode to match equals for HashMap correctness.

One sentence to remember: every class extends Object, which provides toString, equals, hashCode, and getClass – override the first three for meaningful behavior.
